title: The Left Hand of Darkness
author: Ursula K. Le Guin
summary: A human envoy arrives on a frozen world to invite its nations to join a wider alliance. He finds a society whose people have no fixed gender, and a political tangle that forces him to trust a local statesman.
readIf: you like thoughtful science fiction about identity, friendship and being a stranger.
skipIf: you want a lot of action; the plot moves slowly, and the book is mostly about culture and trust.

pairings.reason: Another Le Guin novel about outsiders, politics and ideas, with a sharper debate between two societies.
A more modern work that plays with gender and identity within a vast, bureaucratic space empire.
A short, warm and quiet story about two very different beings learning to understand each other.
